title: A little rule (ch. 73)
hook: Benedict calls it a little rule for beginners

segments.voice: Yesterday, good zeal: honor others first, and carry their weaknesses with patience. Your line was bear with each other.

A man writes out a rule for a whole way of life. Prayer through the day and night, work, food, sleep, the sick, the guests, the tools, the vows, what to do when someone is late for dinner. Then he reaches the final page. A reader might expect a flourish: this is the complete path, follow it and you'll arrive. Benedict writes something close to the opposite. He calls the whole thing a little rule, written for beginners. Today, the Rule's closing chapter.
screen: `A WHOLE WAY OF LIFE, WRITTEN DOWN.` → `THE FINAL PAGE.` → `A LITTLE RULE, FOR BEGINNERS.`

segments.voice: Chapter seventy-three opens with an admission. Benedict wrote this Rule, he says, so that by keeping it, monks might show some measure of good living and a beginning of the monastic life. A beginning, not a finish line. For anyone hurrying on toward something more, there are better teachers. Then he points away from himself. First to Scripture: what page, what word of the Old and New Testaments, he asks, is not a true guide for human life? Then to the writers before him: the holy fathers, the Conferences and Institutes of John Cassian, the lives of the desert monks, the rule of Saint Basil. Next to those, his own work is small. And the last sentence, to whoever is reading: if you are hurrying toward your heavenly home, keep, with Christ's help, this little rule for beginners, and then, under God's protection, you will reach the greater heights he has just named. These past days brought hours for reading, guests received as Christ, kitchen tools treated like vessels of the altar, the sick put first, a promise to stay, the patience to bear each other. All of that, Benedict calls a start. The humility of the ladder chapter turns out to be the author's own. And the beginner isn't someone who will soon stop being one. In the Prologue, Benedict called his monastery a school. Here at the end, he's still enrolling students.
screen: `A BEGINNING, NOT A FINISH LINE.` · `HE POINTS TO SCRIPTURE AND THE FATHERS.` · `THESE PAST DAYS, CALLED A START.` · then, large: `THIS LITTLE RULE FOR BEGINNERS.` · then: `STILL ENROLLING STUDENTS.`

segments.voice: Think of one thing from these chapters you meant to try and didn't, or tried once and dropped: the hour of reading, the guest, the patience. Don't grade yourself; pick it up again now, the way a beginner picks up a pencil on the first day of school, and breathe out the last attempt. If you pray, borrow a psalm line from the Douay-Rheims: "Now have I begun."
A little rule. Benedict's own name for his Rule in its closing chapter: a small rule, written for beginners, pointing beyond itself to Scripture and the fathers. Today's word.
Your line: always beginning. For Benedict, even the whole Rule was only a start. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Benedictines speak of the monastic life as a lifelong beginning, and the Rule, ending with this chapter, is read through again from the Prologue in houses that read it in a cycle.

chat.says: Benedict wrote seventy-three chapters. Did he think his Rule was the complete, perfect path?
options: No. He called it a little rule for beginners and pointed past it to Scripture and earlier teachers.
Yes. He said anyone who kept every chapter exactly would reach perfection within their own lifetime.
No. He said it was only for novices, and that monks should set it aside after their vows.

notes: The Rule is paraphrased. Check the summary of ch. 73: the Rule written so that by observing it monks show some uprightness of life and a beginning of monastic life; for those hastening to perfection, the teachings of the holy fathers; 'what page or word of the Old and New Testament is not a most unerring rule for human life?'; the Conferences and Institutes, the Lives of the Fathers, the rule of our holy father Basil; 'this minimal rule for beginners'; with God's protection you will reach the loftier heights.

Week-end review covers days 1198–1203 (reading, guests, tools, the sick, stability, good zeal). 'The humility of the ladder chapter' refers to day 1194. 'In the Prologue, Benedict called his monastery a school' refers to day 1188 ('a school for the Lord's service').

Practice offers Psalm 76:11 (Douay) 'Now have I begun' as an optional prayer line; it is not quoted in the Rule. Confirm Douay wording ('And I said, Now have I begun: this is the change of the right hand of the most High').
